text:
Maria Nguyen: quick flag — support reported some missing audit fields after the RBAC rollout. End customers are seeing invalid audit events in the UI, and a few got failed validation errors from their ingestion. Can we gate schema changes?

Josh Patel: ugh. Do we know which fields are missing? Is it consumer-side serialization or server-side truncation?

Maria Nguyen: looks like `actor.role` and `target.tenant_id` on ~1.2% of events. Repro is intermittent. I suspect some older clients are still emitting the old shape.

Sophia Li: we should definitely add a schema-gate in the audit ingestion path. Prefer a lightweight validation layer that rejects or tags bad events instead of blocking everyone. Add `schema_version` and `ingest_status` tags.

Kevin O'Connor: +1 for gate. Also worried about perf — validation on every event at peak (100k/s) will add CPU + latency. We need backpressure strategy.

Josh Patel: can we batch-validate? e.g., validate summaries in-line and push full validation to async workers. That gives a fast path for common cases.

Sophia Li: batch-validate + sampling for deep validation. For customer-facing audit events (the ones surfaced in their console) we need strict checks synchronously. Non-customer-facing telemetry can be eventual.

Maria Nguyen: requirement: customer audit views must never show malformed or missing critical fields. So synchronous gate for those; everything else can be queued.

Kevin O'Connor: KMS note: we currently call KMS per-event to encrypt PII fields. That multiplies latency and cost if we validate sync. Two mitigations: envelope encryption (local DEK per worker, KMS only to wrap/unwrap DEK on rotation) OR batch KMS encrypt ops using AEAD with per-shard keys. Both cut KMS QPS.

Josh Patel: envelope approach seems pragmatic. Also consider caching KMS wrap tokens for a short TTL to avoid hitting the KMS for every event. But need to discuss security review.

Sophia Li: on backpressure — infra-bot should create backpressure alerts when audit-queue > 60s or disk-backed queue size > 50% of configured. Also a priority queue: customer-facing events skip long queues.

infra-bot: ALERT configured: audit-queue-lag > 60s -> page eng-infra and eng-security. Link: https://internal.monitoring/redwood/alerts/aur-queue-lag

Kevin O'Connor: indexing cost: Elasticsearch ingestion is a major chunk. If we let malformed events through, they still cost indexing + storage. Schema-gate that tags bad events and routes them to cheaper long-term storage (S3 parquet) for forensic queries.

Maria Nguyen: agreed. plan: (1) implement lightweight sync schema-gate that checks presence of critical fields for customer-facing events, returns 400 and helpful error to clients; (2) tag and route non-critical invalid events to S3 and an async validator job; (3) switch to envelope encryption to reduce KMS QPS; (4) priority queue for customer-facing events + backpressure alerts.

Josh Patel: can we add a fallthrough behavior: if schema-gate fails but the tenant is premium, auto-upgrade to a compatibility-mode and accept with `compat_mode=true` flag so customer console still shows something? We should be explicit.

Sophia Li: I'd prefer explicit opt-in per-tenant. Default should be strict. Auto-upgrade creates audit correctness concerns.

Kevin O'Connor: I'll prototype the validator service this week. Rough sketch: NGINX front -> fast schema-gate in Rust (low overhead) -> route to priority queue or S3. Use `tokio` for batching encrypt calls, use local DEK rotation.

Maria Nguyen: thanks. Can we also add a customer-facing validation endpoint so customers can run their event shape against the prod schema before sending? That might reduce churn.

Josh Patel: +1 on validator endpoint + sample payloads. Also we need a migration plan: publish schema changes in release notes, bump `schema_version` header and deprecate old shapes after 30 days.

Sophia Li: test plan: create a synthetic workload at scale (100k/s) with 1.5% malformed to measure latency, KMS QPS, and queue growth. We'll need cost estimates for ES vs S3 per million events.

Kevin O'Connor: rough cost calc: ES indexing + storage ~ $0.12 / 1k events (high-card fields), S3 cold store ~ $0.01 / 1k. KMS envelope saves ~70% of KMS calls => big savings at scale.

Maria Nguyen: good. I'll open an RFC with the plan and tag infra, devex, product, and security. Action items: Kevin prototype validator, Josh draft migration notes + compat policy, Sophia own test harness + cost numbers.

Kevin O'Connor: noted. ETA prototype PR by EOW.

Josh Patel: I'll draft the customer communication and RFC section for the deprecation schedule.

Sophia Li: I'll start load tests tomorrow and share results in the RFC thread.

Maria Nguyen: thanks all. tagging @product for visibility. We'll reconvene after the RFC comments. :white_check_mark:
